26-qf4-qb-1159.trick: 4% for 5 years is 20%, so the amount is 6/5 of the principal. Take 5/6 of 75,000: 75,000 ÷ 6 = 12,500, and 12,500 × 5 = ₦62,500.

26-qf4-qb-1213.solution: Simple interest I = P × r × t, so r = I ÷ (P × t). Then r = 3,000 ÷ (15,000 × 5) = 3,000 ÷ 75,000 = 0.04, which is 4% per year.
26-qf4-qb-1213.trick: Interest per year is 3,000 ÷ 5 = 600. Then 600 out of 15,000 is 1 in 25, which is 4%.

26-qf4-qb-1345.solution: Simple interest = P × r × t = 40,000 × 0.05 × 3 = ₦6,000. The question asks what the money becomes, so add the principal: 40,000 + 6,000 = ₦46,000.
26-qf4-qb-1345.trick: The money grows, so it becomes more than ₦40,000, and only ₦46,000 is above that. The ₦6,000 option is just the interest.

26-qf4-qb-1602.solution: A 1:200 scale means 1 cm on the plan is 200 cm in real life. So the garden is 3 × 200 = 600 cm by 7 × 200 = 1,400 cm. The area is 600 × 1,400 = 840,000 cm², which is 84 m².
26-qf4-qb-1602.trick: 200 cm is 2 m, so double each side to get metres: 6 m by 14 m. Then 6 × 14 = 84 m², and 84 × 10,000 = 840,000 cm².

26-qf4-qb-1616.trick: Growth is 6% × 5 = 30%, so the principal must be well under 24,000. That rules out ₦46,684, and ₦22,468 would mean only about 7% growth. That leaves ₦18,461.

26-qf4-bm-2004.trick: The gap from the mean is 100 − 84 = 16, which is half of 32. So z = 0.5.

26-qf4-bm-2009.solution: Use the chain rule. The derivative of cos(u) is −sin(u) × u′, and here u = 4x, so u′ = 4. So d/dx cos(4x) = −4sin(4x).
26-qf4-bm-2009.trick: Cos becomes minus sin with the same angle, and the 4 inside comes out to the front. So the answer is −4sin(4x). Do not drop the minus sign.

26-qf4-bm-2017.trick: Squaring and then taking the square root undo each other for positive numbers, so the answer is just 4.

26-qf4-bm-2023.solution: Integrate: f(x) = 3x² − 4x + C. From f(1) = 5 we get 3 − 4 + C = 5, so C = 6. Then f(2) = 3 × 4 − 4 × 2 + 6 = 12 − 8 + 6 = 10.
26-qf4-bm-2023.trick: The slope 6x − 4 is a straight line, so its average from x = 1 to x = 2 is its value at 1.5, which is 5. So f rises by 5, and f(2) = 5 + 5 = 10.

26-qf4-bm-2030.solution: Reading intensity as wave amplitude, each step on the Richter scale is 10 times. The rise in magnitude is log₁₀(100) = 2. So the new magnitude is 6 + 2 = 8.
26-qf4-bm-2030.trick: 100 is 10 × 10, which is two steps of 10 times. So add 2 to the 6 to get 8.

26-qf4-bm-2037.trick: Divide by 3.6. A handy fact is that 36 km/h is 10 m/s, and 90 is 2.5 times 36, so the answer is 25 m/s.

26-qf4-bm-2040.solution: The ratio 2:5 makes 2 + 5 = 7 equal parts. Sugar is 2 of the 7 parts, so sugar = 2/7 × 70 g = 20 g.
26-qf4-bm-2040.trick: 70 ÷ 7 = 10 g per part. Sugar is 2 parts, so 20 g.

26-qf4-bm-2043.solution: The energy stored in a spring is E = ½ × k × x². So E = ½ × 250 × 0.2² = ½ × 250 × 0.04 = 5 J.

26-qf4-bm-2047.solution: Use the product rule (uv)′ = u′v + uv′, with u = 2x² + 1 and v = 3x − 4. So u′ = 4x and v′ = 3. Then f′(x) = 4x(3x − 4) + 3(2x² + 1) = 12x² − 16x + 6x² + 3 = 18x² − 16x + 3.
26-qf4-bm-2047.trick: The highest term of the product is 2x² × 3x = 6x³, so the derivative starts with 3 × 6x² = 18x². Only one option starts with 18x².

26-qf4-bm-2056.solution: Percentage error = |measured − actual| ÷ actual × 100. So it is |24.1 − 25.0| ÷ 25.0 × 100 = 0.9 ÷ 25 × 100 = 3.6%.
26-qf4-bm-2056.trick: Dividing by 25 and multiplying by 100 is the same as multiplying by 4. So 0.9 × 4 = 3.6%.

26-qf4-bm-2060.solution: Percentage yield = actual yield ÷ theoretical yield × 100 = 42.5 ÷ 50.0 × 100 = 0.85 × 100 = 85%.
26-qf4-bm-2060.trick: Double both numbers so the theoretical yield becomes 100. Then 42.5 × 2 = 85, so the yield is 85%.

26-qf4-bm-2065.solution: Complete the square: x² − 12x + 20 = (x − 6)² − 36 + 20 = (x − 6)² − 16. A square is never negative, so the smallest value is −16, reached at x = 6.
26-qf4-bm-2065.trick: The minimum of x² + bx + c is c − (b ÷ 2)². Half of 12 is 6, so the minimum is 20 − 36 = −16.

26-qf4-bm-2071.solution: The volume of a sphere is 4πr³ ÷ 3, so volumes are in the ratio of the cubes of the radii. The radii 2 and 6 are in the ratio 1:3. So the volumes are in the ratio 1³ : 3³ = 1:27.
26-qf4-bm-2071.trick: Simplify the radii to 1:3, then cube both numbers: 1:27.

26-qf4-bm-2075.solution: Reading 80 − 2t as the rate at which water leaves, the volume drained is the integral of 80 − 2t from t = 10 to t = 30. An antiderivative is 80t − t², which is 2,400 − 900 = 1,500 at t = 30 and 800 − 100 = 700 at t = 10. So the volume is 1,500 − 700 = 800 L.
26-qf4-bm-2075.trick: The rate is a straight line, so use average rate × time. At t = 10 the rate is 60 and at t = 30 it is 20, so the average is 40 L/min. Then 40 × 20 minutes = 800 L.

26-qf4-bm-2082.solution: The absolute value (modulus) of z = a + bi is √(a² + b²). So |8 − 6i| = √(8² + (−6)²) = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10.
26-qf4-bm-2082.trick: 8 and 6 are 2 × 4 and 2 × 3, which is the 3, 4, 5 triangle doubled. So the answer is 2 × 5 = 10.

26-qf4-bm-2092.solution: Write y = 5x + 2 and make x the subject. Then y − 2 = 5x, so x = (y − 2)/5. Swapping the letters, the inverse is f⁻¹(x) = (x − 2)/5.
26-qf4-bm-2092.trick: f multiplies by 5 and then adds 2. The inverse undoes that in reverse order: subtract 2, then divide by 5. That gives (x − 2)/5.

26-qf4-bm-2096.solution: Time = volume ÷ rate = 360 litres ÷ 12 litres per minute = 30 minutes.

26-qf4-bm-2099.solution: For a 2 × 2 matrix with rows (a b) and (c d), the determinant is ad − bc. Here a = 2, b = 3, c = 1 and d = 4. So the determinant is 2 × 4 − 3 × 1 = 8 − 3 = 5.
26-qf4-bm-2099.trick: Multiply down the main diagonal and subtract the other diagonal: 8 − 3 = 5.

26-qf4-bm-2102.solution: In a test cross, one map unit (1 cM) is defined as 1% recombinant offspring. So 18 cM means 18% recombinants. Then 18% of 1,000 = 0.18 × 1,000 = 180.
26-qf4-bm-2102.trick: 1 cM is 1%, which is 10 offspring in 1,000. So 18 cM is 18 × 10 = 180.
